report.question: Which mutating operations are safe to run twice? Apply each forward operation twice and each reverse operation twice from an already-applied state, and answer per operation: is the on-disk state after the second application byte-identical to after the first, is the second exit code clean or at least carrying a distinguishable already-applied message, and does any create-if-missing path truncate an existing file?
report.answer: All five mutating operations (install, deploy, migrate, sync, repair) are safe to run twice in both directions on the disposable snapshot engine: install/forward, install/reverse, deploy/forward, deploy/reverse, migrate/forward, migrate/reverse, sync/forward, sync/reverse, repair/forward, repair/reverse. Hash sets after application one and two are equal; second exits are 0 with already-applied when a no-op. create-if-missing left target/user/notes.md byte-identical.
